fields.title: Remove implicit state machines from the Runlimit crates
fields.description:
## Outcome
Every implicit state machine in the five native Runlimit packages and the batter-runlimit adapter is either replaced by a type-level representation (type-state, consuming transition, exhaustive enum, sealed capability or library-owned ordering) or recorded, under ADR-010 review question 5, as application policy, upstream behaviour or inherent persisted state whose in-process decode is made exhaustive. On the canonical native and protected paths no caller has to remember an ordering, a paired call, non-emptiness, a transaction boundary or an outcome to keep a documented invariant.

## Scope and authority
Crates: runlimit-core, runlimit-memory, runlimit-postgres, runlimit-http, runlimit-axum and crates/batter-runlimit. This epic is the catalog and the cross-task decision record; it authorizes no code change, commit, publication or release by itself. Child tasks own delivery scope, acceptance, priority, status and blocker edges. Every native public item is consumer-facing through the facade reexports (batter::runlimit::native, ::memory, ::postgres, ::native_transport), so a public hard cut follows the AGENTS.md rule: a `Breaking:` CHANGELOG entry with before/after code per affected call shape (runlimit/CHANGELOG.md for native packages, root CHANGELOG.md where the facade surface changes), a `Migration:` rustdoc sentence naming the removed item, a recorded `#[deprecated]` shim decision, and a public-API surface diff. Never rewrite published migrations, advisory lock namespaces, shard derivation or subject-key derivation. No second limiter engine. Unix-only.

## Evidence
Static source audit at HEAD 986d294 on 2026-11-08. Every production source file in the six crates and every SQL file under runlimit/runlimit-postgres was read in full; the anchors cited by child tasks were re-read against the working tree. Starting point: repository inventory rows L01-L07 and H03/H04 in docs/evidence/implicit-state-machines-2026-11-05.md; H04 was remediated by batter-jnjj (commit 4639571) and its residue is catalogued here. The audit found 33 raw families: runlimit-core 5, runlimit-memory 9, runlimit-postgres 11, transport and adapter 8. Overlapping families were merged into the child tasks; the finding map and the rejected candidates are recorded in the first comment. No code, tests or live PostgreSQL were executed for the audit: representable-but-invalid states are source-confirmed, not runtime-reproduced, except where a task names an existing test.

## Classification used
Implicit: phase inferred from data (Option, bool, counter, timestamp, collection membership, SQL predicate). Mixed: an explicit state type exists but extra fields or control flow carry essential substates or transition obligations. Protocol: the sequence lives in the program counter and local ownership with no enduring phase value. Configuration, diagnostic counters, ordinary iteration and compiler-generated async state were excluded. A family is debt when a canonical consumer or a third-party backend can compile a known-invalid ordering, pairing, emptiness or omission that the library has enough information to prevent.

## Verification policy
Each task records its ADR-010 invalid-state review, adds the failure-path or `compile_fail` evidence that the removed state is unrepresentable, runs `bash scripts/verify.sh` on the pinned toolchain, runs the named live PostgreSQL tests where the task touches runlimit-postgres, and records actual outcomes in the task. Keep allocation counts on the memory hot path at or below today's (batter-jv92, batter-5618). Fresh-agent usability evaluations are proposals unless executed.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Every child task is closed, each either with a type-level representation that makes the catalogued invalid states unrepresentable and a failure-path or compile_fail test proving it, or with a recorded ADR-010 question-5 justification (application policy, upstream protocol, inherent persisted state with an exhaustive decode). No debug_assert!, expect or doc-only guard protects a phase assumption at any site catalogued here. Every public hard cut shipped with its Breaking: CHANGELOG entry, Migration: rustdoc, shim decision and public-API diff. runlimit/AGENTS.md and crates/batter-runlimit/AGENTS.md invariants name the enforcing type wherever a documented rule became a type rule. Full scripts/verify.sh passed on the delivered tree.

fields.title: Replace the raw check slice with a validated nonempty batch type in Limiter::check_all
fields.description:
## Finding (CORE-4, PG-8; Protocol; public)
`Limiter::check_all(&self, checks: &[Check<'_, Self::Policy>])` (runlimit/runlimit-core/src/limiter.rs:51-54) takes a raw slice. Non-emptiness, one shared `QuotaMode` and no duplicate counter key are runtime checks in `validate_batch` (runlimit/runlimit-core/src/batch.rs:19-57) that every backend must remember to call first (runlimit-memory/src/store.rs:375, runlimit-memory/src/gcra.rs:319, runlimit-postgres/src/lib.rs:350, runlimit-postgres/src/gcra.rs:227). The trait rustdoc invites application-owned delegating enums (limiter.rs:17-19). After validation the shared mode is re-derived from `checks[0]` in runlimit-postgres/src/admission.rs:353-356 and per item in gcra.rs:499-511.

## Representable but invalid
A third-party or application-delegating `Limiter` can implement `check_all` without `validate_batch` and vacuously allow an empty batch or evaluate a mixed-mode batch; every consumer can pass `&[]` and learns only at runtime. Both compile; the guard is a runtime `BatchError` in the backends that remember it. The AGENTS.md rule "an empty batch is a `BatchError::EmptyBatch` failure, never a vacuous allowance" is therefore a backend convention, not a property of the type.

## Proposed remediation
Introduce a validated batch value constructed once, e.g. `Batch<'a, P>::new(&[Check<'a, P>]) -> Result<Batch, BatchError>` carrying the nonempty proof and the shared `QuotaMode` (`Batch::quota_mode()`), and change `Limiter::check_all` to take `&Batch<'_, Self::Policy>`. Keep `BatchTooLarge` as a backend bound (configuration, not structure) or a second bounded step. Remove `checks[0]` derivations and the duplicated per-item mode reads in both backends. Update runlimit-memory, runlimit-postgres, runlimit-axum, batter-runlimit (quota.rs:287, maintenance.rs:328), runlimit/smoke/native_consumer.rs and crates/batter/tests/grants_live/quota_cases.rs in the same change.

## Public hard cut
Yes: `Limiter::check_all` signature and `validate_batch` become the constructor. Ship Breaking: entries in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md and the root CHANGELOG.md facade section, `Migration:` rustdoc on `Batch` naming `validate_batch` and the slice form, and a recorded no-shim decision (the slice form restores the vacuous-allowance state).

## Verification
Existing: runlimit-memory/src/store.rs empty-batch tests, runlimit-postgres/src/lib.rs:735-750, `mixed_quota_modes_fail_before_connecting` (live). Remediation proof: `compile_fail` doctest that `check_all` cannot receive a slice; unit test that `Batch::new(&[])` is `Err(EmptyBatch)`; the delegating-enum example in the trait rustdoc compiles against the new shape.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Limiter::check_all accepts only a validated nonempty single-mode batch type; no backend calls validate_batch as a precondition and no backend indexes checks[0]; a compile_fail doctest proves a slice cannot reach check_all; all four backends, runlimit-axum, batter-runlimit, the smoke consumer and the facade live tests compile against the new shape; Breaking: CHANGELOG entries, Migration: rustdoc and the shim decision are recorded; scripts/verify.sh passes and the live mixed-mode and empty-batch tests still fail closed.

fields.title: Own GCRA batch preflight and commit with an opaque key-bound pending allowance
fields.description:
## Finding (CORE-1, MEM-4, part of PG-10; Protocol with Implicit stored encoding; public backend-author API)
`runlimit_core::gcra::evaluate(check, now_millis, tat_scaled: Option<u128>)` (runlimit/runlimit-core/src/gcra.rs:46-50) returns `Evaluation::Allowed(PendingAllowance)` whose fields `tat_scaled`, `expires_at_millis`, `allowance` are all `pub` and `Copy` (gcra.rs:27-36). The obligation "persist this transition only after batch preflight" is rustdoc (gcra.rs:3-5, 21). The stored counter is `Option<u128>` collapsed by `unwrap_or(scaled_now).max(scaled_now)` (gcra.rs:56). Both in-tree backends sequence it correctly by hand: runlimit-memory/src/gcra.rs:37-47 and 366-417 (preflight loop then commit loop), runlimit-postgres/src/gcra.rs:419-424 and 453 (`Allowed(Vec<PendingAllowance>)`).

## Representable but invalid
A backend can persist one member's pending allowance before evaluating the rest, persist after a sibling denial, apply a token to another counter key, apply it twice, or mutate `tat_scaled` between evaluation and commit. All compile; no guard.

## Proposed remediation
Keep `evaluate` pure. Add a core-owned batch owner, e.g. `gcra::evaluate_batch(checks, now, stored) -> Result<BatchEvaluation, ArithmeticOverflow>` returning either an opaque `CommittableBatch` (private fields; iterates commit records bound to each counter key and evaluation instant; non-`Copy`, consumed once) or `Denied { index, denial }`. Make `PendingAllowance` fields private with accessors, or replace it by the commit record. runlimit-memory folds the token into its shard session (see the memory shard session task); runlimit-postgres binds commit records instead of `allowance.tat_scaled`.

## Public hard cut
Yes for `PendingAllowance` field access and any direct construction. Breaking: entry in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md with before/after, `Migration:` rustdoc on the replacement naming `PendingAllowance`, no shim (public fields restore the unordered-commit state). Arithmetic and persisted keys are unchanged.

## Verification
Existing: runlimit-memory `matches_rational_token_bucket_reference_across_small_parameter_space`, `arithmetic_preflight_preserves_expired_entries_and_emits_only_failure`; runlimit-postgres/tests/gcra.rs and gcra/clock.rs (live). Remediation proof: core unit test that a batch with one denied member yields no commit record; `compile_fail` doctest that a commit record cannot be constructed, copied or mutated outside core.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: runlimit_core::gcra exposes one batch evaluation owner whose allowed result is an opaque, non-Copy, key-bound set of commit records consumed once, and a denied result that carries no commit records; PendingAllowance has no public fields; both backends persist only through the commit records; compile_fail evidence and the one-denied-member test exist; Breaking: CHANGELOG, Migration: rustdoc and the shim decision are recorded; live GCRA tests pass unchanged in semantics.

fields.title: Make attempt completion an exhaustive reset-or-backoff enum
fields.description:
## Finding (CORE-2; Implicit; public)
`AttemptCompletion { outcome, consecutive_failures: u32, retry_after: Delay }` (runlimit/runlimit-core/src/attempts.rs:172-176) admits two shapes that a runtime check in `AttemptCompletion::new` (attempts.rs:186-207) sorts into valid or `AttemptCompletionError`: success requires zero failures and zero delay; failure or abandonment requires both nonzero. The accessors `consecutive_failures()` and `retry_after()` answer for both shapes with a plain `u32` and `Delay`, which runlimit/AGENTS.md names as debt ("do not add accessors that answer for several outcomes at once").

## Representable but invalid
`AttemptCompletion::new(Success, 1, Delay::new(Duration::ZERO))` compiles and fails at runtime (runlimit/smoke/native_consumer.rs:131 demonstrates it). The memory backend converts the `Result` into a panic path with `.expect("policy transition produces consistent completion metadata")` (runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/attempts.rs:204-206); the PostgreSQL backend maps it to a `StorageInvariant` (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs:381-385).

## Proposed remediation
`enum AttemptCompletion { Reset, Backoff { kind: FailureKind /* Failure | Abandoned */, consecutive_failures: NonZeroU32, retry_after: Delay /* nonzero by a validated constructor */ } }`. Delete `AttemptCompletionError` and the fallible constructor. The memory backend builds the enum directly and loses its `expect`; the PostgreSQL row decode keeps a `StorageInvariant` arm only for a row whose stored shape cannot be expressed (nonzero failures with zero delay). `AttemptObservation::Completed` and the batter-runlimit runner (crates/batter-runlimit/src/attempts.rs:380, 404) consume the enum.

## Public hard cut
Yes: constructor signature, accessor removal, `AttemptObservation::Completed` payload shape. Breaking: entry in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md with before/after, `Migration:` rustdoc naming `AttemptCompletion::new` and `AttemptCompletionError`, no shim (the old constructor is the fallible shape being removed). The type is not serialized, so no wire impact.

## Verification
Existing: runlimit-memory/tests/attempts.rs, runlimit-postgres/tests/attempts.rs (live), crates/batter-runlimit/tests/attempts_live.rs (live). Remediation proof: `compile_fail` doctest that a backoff completion cannot carry a zero delay or zero failures; the memory `expect` is gone; the PostgreSQL malformed-row test still yields `StorageInvariant`.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: AttemptCompletion is an exhaustive enum with no fallible constructor and no accessor that answers for both shapes; AttemptCompletionError is removed; runlimit-memory has no expect on completion construction; the PostgreSQL decode retains only the storage-invariant arm; compile_fail evidence exists; Breaking: CHANGELOG, Migration: rustdoc and shim decision recorded; memory, PostgreSQL (live) and batter-runlimit attempt tests pass.

fields.title: Make the PostgreSQL low-level attempt claim and finish protocol transaction-owned
fields.description:
## Finding (PG-1, CORE-3, L05, L07; Protocol, public temporal obligation)
`runlimit_postgres::attempts::low_level::{claim_in, finish_in, complete_in}` (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs:411-466) accept any `E: Executor<'e, Database = Postgres>`. The claim binds `pg_current_xact_id()` and the SQL fence in runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempt_complete.sql compares it; the obligations "hold the same transaction through finish and commit", "an autocommit executor produces a claim unusable in subsequent transactions", "rollback on every error" are rustdoc (attempts.rs:388-407). `StagedAttemptCompletion::Applied(AttemptCompletion)` (runlimit/runlimit-core/src/attempts.rs:231-238) is structurally identical to the acknowledged `AttemptCompletionResult::Applied` (attempts.rs:222-229), so an unacknowledged completion already is an `AttemptCompletion` and can be published through `AttemptObservation::Completed` before commit. The protected runner (crates/batter-runlimit/src/attempts.rs:352-384) sequences claim, application decision, finish and acknowledgement correctly by hand.

## Representable but invalid
All compile with no Rust guard: `claim_in(&pool, receipt)` (row lock released at statement end, dead xact id, every later finish is `Stale` at the database); `finish_in` on another executor than the claim (`Stale`, proven by crates/batter/tests/grants_live/quota_cases.rs:293 and the native `claim_is_transaction_fenced…` live test); host commit between claim and finish (lease stays live until expiry, moved receipt gone); application writes before the claim; emitting `Completed` from a staged value before commit.

## Design constraint
The protected runner obtains its executor from batter-sqlx's atomic scope (`PgScopedSql::executor() -> impl Executor` over `&mut PgConnection`, crates/batter-sqlx/src/atomic/scope.rs:38), not from `sqlx::Transaction`. The remediation therefore needs a transaction witness that both `&mut sqlx::Transaction<'_, Postgres>` (savepoints included, keeping tests/attempts.rs:738-830 semantics) and batter-sqlx's scoped session can present, for example a sealed `InTransaction` trait implemented by both, or a claim type that owns the transaction and exposes `&mut Transaction` for application work with one consuming `finish(outcome)`.

## Proposed remediation
Require the witness on `claim_in`/`finish_in`/`complete_in` so an autocommit executor does not compile; make the staged payload opaque (`StagedAttemptCompletion::Applied(StagedCompletion)` with private fields and a single consuming `acknowledge(self, CommitProof) -> AttemptCompletion`, the proof produced by the owning commit path), so `AttemptObservation::Completed` cannot be built from a staged value. Move crates/batter-runlimit/src/attempts.rs and crates/batter/tests/grants_live/quota_cases.rs in the same change; the fence evidence test must use a second transaction rather than a pool.

## Public hard cut
Yes: three public function signatures and the `Applied` payload. Breaking: entries in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md and the facade section of the root CHANGELOG.md, `Migration:` rustdoc naming `claim_in`/`finish_in` executor forms and `StagedAttemptCompletion::Applied(AttemptCompletion)`, no shim (the old shapes restore the autocommit and pre-commit-publication states). Persisted protocol unchanged.

## Verification
Existing (live): `completion_and_application_writes_rollback_together`, `claim_is_transaction_fenced_and_survives_lease_elapsed_while_locked`, `cancelled_host_transaction_does_not_reset_retry_state`, `rolled_back_savepoint_invalidates_claim_even_in_same_transaction`; crates/batter-runlimit/tests/attempts_live.rs. Remediation proof: `compile_fail` doctests for `claim_in(&pool, …)` and for building `Completed` from a staged value; the protected runner compiles against the witness.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: claim_in, finish_in and complete_in cannot be called with an autocommit executor (compile_fail evidence); the staged completion payload cannot become an AttemptCompletion or an AttemptObservation::Completed without the owning commit path's acknowledgement; the protected runner and the facade live grants tests compile and pass against the new shape with the fence test using a second transaction; Breaking: CHANGELOG, Migration: rustdoc and shim decision recorded; the named live PostgreSQL tests pass.

fields.title: Derive failure observation consumption from the failing phase instead of a free argument
fields.description:
## Finding (CORE-5, L06 vocabulary; Mixed; public backend-author API)
`AdmissionObservation::failed_check` and `failed_batch` (runlimit/runlimit-core/src/observation.rs:157-193) take a free `ConsumptionStatus` (observation.rs:136-144: `Consumed`, `NotConsumed`, `PossiblyConsumed`). Which value is true depends on where in its transaction protocol the backend failed; that phase is encoded elsewhere (runlimit-postgres `ConnectionOutcome` and the cancellation guard). The observer contract "backends invoke observers only after releasing internal locks and finalizing database transactions" is rustdoc (observation.rs:11-16).

## Representable but invalid
`failed_check(&check, ConsumptionStatus::Consumed, ..)` for a pre-commit failure, or `NotConsumed` after a lost commit acknowledgement, both compile; no guard. runlimit/smoke/native_consumer.rs:63 constructs a failed batch observation directly.

## Proposed remediation
Phase-owned constructors with no free status, e.g. `failed_before_commit(..)` (always `NotConsumed`) and `failed_after_commit_request(..)` (always `PossiblyConsumed`), or constructors that take a backend error type which already knows its consumption (PostgreSQL `CheckError::consumption()` exists at runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs:208). `Consumed` remains reachable only from a completed allowance. Coordinate with the PostgreSQL disposition classifier task so the classification is derived once.

## Public hard cut
Yes if the free parameter is removed from the two constructors. Breaking: entry in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md with before/after, `Migration:` rustdoc naming `failed_check`/`failed_batch` with `ConsumptionStatus`, shim decision recorded (likely none: the free parameter is the invalid shape).

## Verification
Existing: observation.rs unit test `failure_factories_preserve_consumption_and_couple_policy_metadata`; runlimit-postgres/tests/postgres.rs consumption-status cases (live). Remediation proof: a failure observation built from a pre-commit error type cannot carry `PossiblyConsumed` (type-level or exhaustive unit test over every backend error class).

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: No public failure-observation constructor accepts a free ConsumptionStatus; the status is derived from the failing phase or error class in one place per backend; the smoke consumer compiles; Breaking: CHANGELOG, Migration: rustdoc and shim decision recorded; observation unit tests and the live consumption-status cases pass.

fields.title: Own the attempt lease transition as one pure function in runlimit-core
fields.description:
## Finding (L04, L05, MEM-8, PG-3; Implicit, duplicated across backends)
The attempt lease lifecycle (absent, leased, lease expired and counted as a failure, backoff, quiet-period reset, eligible, reclaimable) is evaluated twice by sequential mutation of loose locals, once per backend: runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/attempts.rs:20-26 (`Entry { failures, last_failure, retry_at, lease: Option<(u64, Duration)> }`) with `reconcile`/`fail`/`deny` at 207-239, and runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs:246-285 (`failures`, `last_failure`, `retry` mutated through ordered `if`s). The backoff schedule exists three times: `AttemptPolicy::delay` in Rust for both backends' expired-lease path and SQL `LEAST($6, $5 * power(2, LEAST(failures,63)))` in runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempt_complete.sql:11 for completion. runlimit/AGENTS.md requires the memory and PostgreSQL backends to implement the same semantics, yet no attempt-equivalence test exists (only fixed windows have `memory_and_postgres_share_fixed_window_transition_semantics`).

## Representable but invalid
Order-dependent blocks (swapping the expired-lease and quiet-reset steps changes semantics) compile in both backends; `failures == 0` with a future `retry_at`, or a live lease next to a stale `retry_at`, are representable; the two delay formulas can drift silently. None of this is unit-testable for PostgreSQL without a database.

## Proposed remediation
Add to `runlimit_core::attempts` one pure, storage-free transition owner, e.g. `enum AttemptState { Absent, Leased { until, failures, .. }, Backoff { failures: NonZeroU32, retry_at, last_failure }, Quiet { since } }` with `AttemptState::admit(self, policy, now) -> Admit::{Denied(AttemptDenial), Lease(..)}` and `AttemptState::complete(self, policy, now, outcome) -> (AttemptState, AttemptCompletion)`, plus the single delay derivation. Both backends decode storage into `AttemptState`, call the transition, and write the result back. This is additive backend-author API; the two adoption tasks consume it.

## Public hard cut
No (additive). New public API needs rustdoc, an example and a `runlimit/CHANGELOG.md` Added entry.

## Verification
Remediation proof: exhaustive unit tests over every state and event (including an expired lease observed at completion, the quiet-period reset, saturation at the cap); a property or table test that the Rust delay equals the SQL formula for failures 0..=64 against the policy bounds.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: runlimit_core::attempts owns one explicit attempt state enum and one pure transition function with the single backoff-delay derivation; its unit tests cover every state and event and prove the delay formula matches attempt_complete.sql across the policy range; rustdoc and an example exist; the Added entry is in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md; no backend behaviour changes in this task.

fields.title: Represent memory attempt entries as the explicit lease state and reconcile on completion
fields.description:
## Finding (MEM-8, L04; Implicit; private with observable behaviour)
runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/attempts.rs keeps `Entry { failures, last_failure, retry_at, lease }` (20-26); `last_failure` is initialised to admission time so it doubles as last activity; `reconcile` (213-229) turns an expired lease into a failure and resets quiet entries, but only `admit` calls it. `complete` (165-201) matches a live lease or falls to `_ => Stale`, so completing an already-expired receipt returns `Stale` without applying the abandonment. Between lease expiry and the next `admit`, the entry's failure state is stale, and observers never see an expiry-driven `Completed(Abandoned)`, only `Stale`.

## Proposed remediation
Store the core `AttemptState` from the shared transition task and run reconciliation on every access path, including `complete`, so an expired-lease completion applies the abandonment immediately and the following `admit` observes `Backoff`. Document the observation sequence change (an abandonment completion may now be emitted). Keep the 16-key cleanup scan and allocation behaviour of batter-jv92/batter-5618.

## Public hard cut
No. Behavioural note in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md.

## Verification
Existing: runlimit-memory/tests/attempts.rs (`failure_delays_escalate_cap_and_success_resets`, `quiet_period_resets_failures_and_abandonment_counts`, `backwards_clock_does_not_shorten_delay_or_clear_active_lease`, `quiet_expiry_never_evicts_a_longer_active_lease`). New: completing an expired receipt applies the failure immediately and the next `admit` sees `Backoff`, not a second expiry; a memory-versus-PostgreSQL attempt-equivalence test shared with the PostgreSQL adoption task.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The memory attempt store holds the core AttemptState and performs every transition through the shared function; completing an expired receipt applies the abandonment and the next admit observes Backoff; the new failure-path test and the existing attempt tests pass; allocation counts on admit are unchanged or lower; the behaviour change is recorded in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md.

fields.title: Decode PostgreSQL attempt rows into the explicit lease state and evaluate with the shared transition
fields.description:
## Finding (PG-3, L05; Implicit; private, persisted)
runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs:246-285 decodes `failures`, `last_failure_ms`, `retry_at_ms`, `lease_until_ms` into loose locals and evaluates them through ordered `if`s (live lease then Busy; expired lease then failures+1 and `retry = until + delay`; quiet elapsed then reset; `now < retry` then Backoff; else insert or update). The row shape pairs `lease_until_ms`/`lease_token` under `CHECK ((lease_until_ms IS NULL) = (lease_token IS NULL))` in attempts-migrations/20260921000001_create_runlimit_attempts.sql:16, and `retry_at_ms < last_failure_ms` is unconstrained. Guards today: `StorageInvariant` on negative or oversized counts only.

## Proposed remediation
Decode each row once into the core `AttemptState` (invalid combinations become a pre-commit `StorageInvariant`), evaluate with the shared transition function, and bind its outputs. Make the completion delay a single owner: either compute it in Rust from the same function and bind it into attempt_complete.sql, or keep SQL as the only owner for both paths; do not keep two formulas. Published migrations stay byte-identical; a new statement, if needed, is forward-only.

## Public hard cut
No. Persisted schema unchanged.

## Verification
Existing (live): `failure_escalation_cap_and_success_reset`, `expired_receipt_cannot_clear_newer_failures`, `capacity_is_bounded_and_quiet_expiry_reclaims_slots`, `malformed_admission_state_is_a_semantic_storage_invariant`. New: a memory-versus-PostgreSQL attempt-equivalence test over a scripted sequence (admit, expire, complete, quiet, re-admit) asserting identical denials, completions and delays.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: PostgreSQL attempt admission decodes rows into the core AttemptState and evaluates through the shared transition; one delay derivation exists for admission and completion; invalid row combinations surface as pre-commit StorageInvariant; the new memory-versus-PostgreSQL attempt-equivalence live test and the named live tests pass; no published migration changed.

fields.title: Replace shard presence and active-entry predicates with one exhaustive entry state and fail closed on index divergence
fields.description:
## Finding (MEM-2, MEM-5, L01, L03; Implicit; private)
`Shard::contains_key` (runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/shards.rs:100-102) is true for an expired-but-unpruned entry while `active_entry` (shards.rs:104-107) returns `None` for it. Capacity checks use the former (store.rs:318, 430; gcra.rs:254, 386), quota checks the latter, so "absent / active / expired-present" is a three-state value read through two booleans. The dual index `Shard { entries, expirations }` (shards.rs:61-67) is kept aligned by `replace` and `prune_expired` with `debug_assert!` only (shards.rs:137, 143, 162-166); release builds continue past divergence because `removed.is_some()` is counted, not enforced (shards.rs:167).

## Representable but invalid
Using one predicate where the other is meant compiles (counting an expired key as a pending insertion, or denying capacity to a refreshable key); an entry without an expiration or vice versa is representable and silently tolerated in release.

## Proposed remediation
One `Shard::lookup(key, now) -> EntryState<'_, E>::{Absent, Expired { expires_at }, Active { value, expires_at }}` and removal of `contains_key`/`active_entry` from production code; either make index divergence fail closed in release with a shard-invariant error behaving like `PoisonedShardError`, or collapse to one `ExpiringMap` whose only mutators maintain both indexes.

## Public hard cut
No.

## Verification

fields.title: Own the memory shard session and batch preflight-to-commit with a consuming token shared by both stores
fields.description:
## Finding (MEM-1, MEM-3, MEM-6, L01, L02; Protocol; private, duplicated)
Fixed-window `Shard<Entry>::quota_denial` returns `Option<QuotaDenial>` and `consume` re-reads the entry behind `debug_assert!(check.cost <= remaining, "quota denial must be checked before consumption")` (runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/store.rs:28-58); release builds saturate and emit an allowance with `available = 0`, i.e. silent over-admission if the order is wrong. The per-check session (lock, clamp `latest_observed_millis` at shards.rs:64 and 92-98, record, bounded prune, decide, consume) is ordered by control flow in store.rs:304-311 and gcra.rs:241-250, with a deliberate but unencoded difference (GCRA evaluates overflow before recording). The batch two-phase (preflight loop with `pending_insertions`, then a mirrored commit loop) is duplicated in store.rs:413-458 and gcra.rs:366-417, and `.expect("batch validation rejected the empty batch")` (store.rs:455, gcra.rs:414) depends on `validate_batch` having run earlier.

## Representable but invalid
Calling `consume` without a preceding denial check, pruning before recording, recording a clamped time the evaluation did not use, or committing without (or in a different order than) preflight all compile; only tests and a debug assertion guard them.

## Proposed remediation
In shards.rs, a private `ShardSession` constructor that performs clamp, record and bounded prune once and returns `(session, CleanupEffect)`; `evaluate(check, now) -> Evaluation::{Denied(QuotaDenial), Allowed(PendingConsumption)}` with `consume(PendingConsumption)` taking a non-`Copy`, crate-private token by value; a generic `Preflighted<'a, E, T>` owning `LockedShards`, cleanup effects and per-check tokens, built by one shared `preflight` whose denial exits return before the value exists, with `commit()` its only consumer. GCRA's arithmetic preflight stays an explicit step before the session. Fold the core GCRA commit records in when that task lands. Delete the debug assertion and the empty-batch `expect`.

## Public hard cut
No.

## Constraints
Allocation count on the hot path at or below today's (batter-jv92, batter-5618); lock order and the capacity-denial rollback semantics unchanged.

## Verification
Existing: `enforces_quota_and_reports_exact_retry_duration`, `single_check_matches_a_one_element_batch_across_state_transitions`, `a_denied_batch_does_not_consume_other_checks`, `batch_preflight_preserves_validation_capacity_and_lock_precedence`, `storage_capacity_denial_rolls_back_earlier_batch_members`, `concurrent_cross_shard_batches_lock_consistently_and_never_over_admit`, `regressing_clocks_cannot_refill_quota_early`, `arithmetic_preflight_preserves_expired_entries_and_emits_only_failure`. New: one shared test proving a denied preflight leaves `used()` and every stored value unchanged across both stores; the consume entry point requires the token (compile-level).

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: runlimit-memory has one shard session owner and one preflight-to-commit owner used by both the fixed-window and GCRA stores; consumption requires a consuming token produced only by evaluation; the debug_assert and the empty-batch expect are gone; allocation counts on check and check_all are unchanged or lower; the named tests and the new shared denied-preflight test pass.

fields.title: Make memory receipt and poison-recovery outcomes unignorable
fields.description:
## Finding (MEM-9, MEM-7, L03, L04; Implicit; public)
`MemoryAttemptReceipt { store: Weak<..>, key, generation }` (runlimit/runlimit-memory/src/attempts.rs:35-40) has no `#[must_use]` and no `Drop`; abandonment is inferred later from lease expiry ("Dropped receipts expire as failures", attempts.rs:1); completing on another store is caught at runtime by `Weak::ptr_eq` (attempts.rs:172-178) and reported as `Stale`. `recover_poisoned` (store.rs:474-493, shards.rs:371-395) discards every counter in a poisoned shard and returns a bare `usize`, so `Err(PoisonedShardError) => { store.recover_poisoned(); retry }` is a one-line automatic recovery that over-admits, which the repository's "never retry because an error sounds transient" rule argues against.

## Representable but invalid
Dropping a receipt compiles silently (subject stays Busy until expiry, then counts as a failure: conservative but never explicit); completing on another store compiles and yields `Stale`; ignoring the recovery result compiles.

## Proposed remediation
(a) `#[must_use = "complete the receipt or the attempt counts as a failure at lease expiry"]` on the receipt (non-breaking). (b) Replace the `usize` with a `#[must_use]` typed recovery report (shards rebuilt, counters discarded) and state in rustdoc that recovery is an operator decision, not an error-handling branch (public hard cut: return type, reexported through batter::runlimit::memory). (c) Assess branding the receipt to its limiter so cross-store completion does not compile (lifetime or store-id parameter); record the decision either way, since the protected path (batter-runlimit) uses the PostgreSQL store and the memory API is the disclosed native escape hatch.

## Public hard cut
Yes for (b): Breaking: entry in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md with before/after, `Migration:` rustdoc naming the `usize` return, shim decision recorded. (a) is additive. (c) only if adopted.

## Verification
Existing: tests/attempts.rs stale and other-store tests; `a_poisoned_default_shard_remains_fail_closed`, `explicit_recovery_resets_only_poisoned_shards_behind_an_arc`, `recovery_reopens_every_shard_poisoned_by_an_unwinding_batch`. New: a `deny(unused_must_use)` consumer probe for the dropped receipt and the ignored recovery report; a `compile_fail` doctest if (c) is adopted.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: MemoryAttemptReceipt is #[must_use] with the expiry consequence in its message; recover_poisoned returns a #[must_use] typed report; the branding decision for cross-store completion is recorded with its reason; the must_use consumer probe exists; Breaking: CHANGELOG, Migration: rustdoc and shim decision recorded for the return-type cut; memory attempt and poison tests pass.

fields.title: Require a shaped decision to finalize a PostgreSQL check transaction and classify connection disposition once
fields.description:
## Finding (PG-5, PG-6, L06; Protocol and Implicit; private)
The rule "build the decision from the response before the transaction is finalized" (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/admission.rs:235-240, lib.rs:56-59) is enforced only by statement order in `run_check_transaction_inner` (admission.rs:366-383) and runlimit-postgres/src/gcra.rs:409-444; the denied path reaches `transaction.inner.rollback()` directly (admission.rs:379) although `CheckTransaction` documents that no method exposes its inner transaction (admission.rs:263-265). `ConnectionCancellationGuard { armed: bool }` (lib.rs:508-549) is disarmed by `reuse(&mut self)` or consuming `finish`; `ConnectionOutcome<Result<T, E>>` (lib.rs:111-125) yields four combinations, and the timeout-closes versus server-error-reuses classification is repeated at admission.rs:409-437, maintenance.rs:67-88 and 110-128, and attempts.rs:339-342. `PostgresAttemptLimiter::migrate` ignores the guard and always closes (attempts.rs:111) while the other two migrators reuse on success (lib.rs:279-293, gcra.rs:179-190). The public `TimedOutBeforeCommit` variant carries two dispositions (client deadline closes, server 57014/55P03 reuses), so disposition cannot be derived from the public error and is re-decided per site.

## Representable but invalid
Committing before shaping (turning a malformed response into a possibly-consumed error), `Reusable(Err(CommitTimedOut))`, `MustClose(Ok(allowed))`, and using the connection after `reuse()` all compile; no guard. `single_decisions_are_shaped_before_the_transaction_is_finalized` tests shaping, not its position relative to commit.

## Proposed remediation
Make `CheckTransaction::commit(self, decision: D)` and `deny(self, decision: D)` the only finalizers, returning `ConnectionOutcome<D>`, so finalizing without a shaped decision does not compile; remove the direct `inner.rollback()` path. Replace `reuse` with one private classifier (error origin to disposition) applied once in `finish`, used by every check, maintenance and migrate path, including the attempt migrator. Coordinate with the core failure-observation task so consumption and disposition derive from the same classification.

## Public hard cut
No.

## Verification
Existing (live): `malformed_upsert_response_is_rejected_before_commit`, `undecodable_upsert_field_is_storage_invariant_before_commit`, `cleanup_timeout_cannot_late_commit_and_releases_pool_slot`, `row_lock_timeout_releases_single_connection_pool_slot_without_consuming_quota`, `cancelling_migration_discards_its_session_lock`; unit `finish_denied_transaction` tests at lib.rs:756-805. New: unit tests of the classifier for every error class; the API shape makes commit-before-shape unrepresentable.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: CheckTransaction can be finalized only through consuming commit(decision) or deny(decision), with no direct inner rollback; one private classifier decides connection disposition for every check, maintenance and migrate path, and reuse(&mut self) is gone; classifier unit tests cover every error class; the named live tests pass.

fields.title: Own maintenance transactions with library-ordered timeout refresh and typed GCRA cleanup steps
fields.description:
## Finding (PG-7, L06; Protocol; private)
The check path refreshes PostgreSQL per-statement server timeouts inside `CheckTransaction::prepare` before every statement (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/admission.rs:285-315). The cleanup paths use a raw `sqlx::Transaction` and call `set_maintenance_server_timeouts` by hand: once in maintenance.rs:47-51, three times across runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/gcra.rs:545-593, then again inside `commit_maintenance` (maintenance.rs:108-122). GCRA cleanup also requires the fixed order lock shards, advance the watermark, delete (gcra.rs:60-100).

## Representable but invalid
Adding a maintenance statement without a preceding refresh compiles and silently runs under a stale server timeout; reordering the GCRA watermark and delete statements compiles.

## Proposed remediation
A `MaintenanceTransaction` mirroring `CheckTransaction` (or `CheckTransaction` generic over phase and error type) so the refresh is library-owned per statement, and a typed three-step GCRA cleanup whose steps consume each other. Build on the disposition classifier from the check-transaction task.

## Public hard cut
No.

## Verification
Existing (live): `successive_lock_waits_share_the_remaining_server_deadline` covers the check path only; attempts/cleanup.rs and postgres/cleanup_plan.rs tests. New: a GCRA cleanup test asserting the second and third statements observe the remaining budget; the typed steps make reordering unrepresentable.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Every maintenance statement in runlimit-postgres runs through a transaction owner that refreshes server timeouts before it, with no hand-called refresh in cleanup code; GCRA cleanup steps are typed and ordered by consumption; the new cleanup budget test and the existing live cleanup tests pass.

fields.title: Type attempt admission terminals and report the actual statement phase
fields.description:
## Finding (PG-4, PG-11, L05; Mixed; private with public error content)
Attempt admission chooses its terminal per call site: `finish_denial` rolls back and undoes the inline 16-row cleanup (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/attempts.rs:321-329); `finish_capacity_denial` commits so cleanup persists and maps a failed commit into a certain denial with `outcome.map(|_| denial)` (attempts.rs:330-343); the admitted path commits at 317. `CheckTransaction::commit`/`deny` are agnostic to decision kind. A `CommitOutcomeUnknown` on the capacity path is therefore reported as a certain `StorageCapacity` denial and observed as `AttemptObservation::Denied`, never `CommitUncertain`, although the cleanup deletions are uncertain. Fixed-window and GCRA limiters expose `cleanup_expired`; the attempt limiter has only this inline cleanup. Separately, every attempt statement reports `const PHASE: CheckPhase = CheckPhase::AcquiringCounterRowLocks` (attempts.rs:34; used at 184, 224-241, 288-316), so an attempt timeout always names a fixed-window phase.

## Proposed remediation
Typed consuming terminals (`commit_allowed(decision)`, `rollback_denied(decision)`, and an explicitly named side-effecting `commit_cleanup_then_deny` that surfaces an uncertain commit as uncertain), or move expired-row reclamation into `PostgresAttemptLimiter::cleanup_expired` so every denial rolls back uniformly (behaviour change under lowered caps; record the choice). Add attempt-specific phase variants (additive to `CheckPhase`, semver-signaled under the no-`non_exhaustive` rule) supplied per statement.

## Public hard cut
No removal; new `CheckPhase` variants are a semver-signaled addition recorded in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md.

## Verification
Existing (live): `lowered_capacity_counts_live_slots_outside_the_new_allocation_interval`, `lowered_capacity_reclaims_expired_rows_across_denied_cleanup_batches`. New: a test that an uncertain commit on the capacity path surfaces as uncertain (or is impossible after the move); a timeout test asserting the reported phase per attempt statement.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Attempt admission terminals are typed and chosen by decision kind, an uncertain commit on the capacity path is never reported or observed as a certain denial, the convergence decision under lowered caps is recorded, each attempt statement reports its own phase, and the new and named live tests pass.

fields.title: Decode persisted fixed-window and GCRA counters into explicit stored states and derive their predicates once
fields.description:
## Finding (PG-9, PG-10, L01, L02; Implicit; persisted and private)
Fixed windows: the activity predicate `window_expires_at > now` and the fullness predicate are duplicated across `BATCH_PREFLIGHT_SQL` (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/protocol.rs:170-185), the `BATCH_UPSERT_SQL` CASE and WHERE (protocol.rs:224-244) and the cleanup cutoff (cleanup_expired_by_key.sql); slot need is "row absent" in `BATCH_CAPACITY_LOCK_SQL` (protocol.rs:112-121); Rust re-derives expiry in admission.rs:825-833 and `PendingAllowance::new` guards `used <= limit` on read (admission.rs:163-177) because the limit is not stored. GCRA: the `(Option<tat>, Option<expires>)` tuple decode (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/gcra.rs:474-483) admits mismatched Some/None rejected at runtime; "active" is `.filter(expires > now)` (gcra.rs:492-494) while "needs a slot" is `stored.is_none()` (gcra.rs:512); `evaluate` keeps pushing allowances after the first denial (gcra.rs:497-527) with the mode encoded by `denial.is_some()`.

## Proposed remediation
Keep the persisted state (inherent). Decode each row once into `StoredWindow::{Absent, Active, Expired}` and `StoredGcra::{Absent, Active { tat }, Expired}`; derive the three fixed-window statements from one predicate definition (Rust-side composition or a new forward-only SQL function; the imported cleanup_expired.sql stays byte-identical as provenance); stop GCRA evaluation at the first denial and consume core commit records when that task lands.

## Public hard cut
No. Migrations unchanged.

## Verification
Existing (live): `fixed_window_transitions`, `expired_rows_hold_capacity_until_cleanup_commits`, `cleanup_uses_an_indexable_cutoff_and_skips_locked_rows`, `memory_and_postgres_share_fixed_window_transition_semantics`, tests/gcra.rs, tests/gcra/clock.rs. New: unit tests of both decoders over every tuple shape; a test that evaluation stops at the first denial.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: PostgreSQL fixed-window and GCRA rows are decoded once into exhaustive stored-state enums, the fixed-window activity and fullness predicates have one definition, GCRA evaluation stops at the first denial, decoder unit tests cover every row shape, no migration changed, and the named live tests pass.

fields.title: Decide whether native PostgreSQL limiters need an installed-schema constructor
fields.description:
## Finding (PG-2; Protocol with Implicit persisted phase; public)
`PostgresLimiter::new` (runlimit/runlimit-postgres/src/lib.rs, constructor near 240-260), `PostgresAttemptLimiter::new` (attempts.rs:81) and `PostgresGcraLimiter::new` (gcra.rs:149) return immediately usable limiters; `migrate` (lib.rs:279-293, attempts.rs:109, gcra.rs:179) is a separate optional call, and three install routes exist per limiter (`migrate`, the raw `MIGRATOR` statics, vendored SQL constants). The installation level (0.1 fixed windows versus 0.2 bounded cardinality) exists only as table and trigger presence; `BATCH_CAPACITY_LOCK_SQL` assumes `runlimit_capacity_shards`.

## Representable but invalid
A limiter serving traffic before any migration, or against a 0.1-only vendored install, compiles; the runtime guard is a per-request `CheckError::DefinitelyNotConsumed(undefined_table)` (fail closed, but repeated and late). No probe exists in the native crate; Batter's facade has read-only Runlimit installation validation (batter-wloc).

## Deliverable
An ADR-010 question-5 decision with evidence: either (a) add an `installed(pool, config).await -> Result<Self, …>` constructor that verifies the expected relations and triggers read-only and returns the usable limiter, keeping `new` as a disclosed low-level seam for hosts that vendored SQL (one owner for the probe; do not duplicate batter-wloc), or (b) record that installation is application policy because a host-owned migrator legitimately installs the schema out of band, and point the native rustdoc at the facade verification. Record the decision in this task and in runlimit/AGENTS.md.

## Verification
If (a): a live test that the verified constructor refuses an empty or 0.1-only schema with a typed error before any check; `migration_upgrades_the_published_0_1_table_additively` and `migration_coexists_with_an_ignore_missing_host_and_discards_errors` unchanged. If (b): rustdoc and guide updates only.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision with evidence: either the native crates expose a verified installed-schema constructor with a live test refusing empty and 0.1-only schemas, and `new` is documented as the low-level seam, or the migrate-before-use obligation is recorded as application policy in the task, runlimit/AGENTS.md and the constructor rustdoc, naming the facade verification as the protected owner.

fields.title: Seal the runlimit-axum Admissions request extension
fields.description:
## Finding (ADP-1; Implicit; public and wire) `Admission::new` (runlimit/runlimit-axum/src/lib.rs:159-168), `Admissions::new`, `Admissions::push` and `From for Admissions` (lib.rs:203-262) are public; the layer appends to any inbound collection or inserts a new one (lib.rs:457-463), and `Admissions::get` returns the outermost match (lib.rs:226-228). runlimit/AGENTS.md requires that a layer never overwrite another layer's entry, but nothing restricts who may create entries. ## Representable but invalid An outer non-layer middleware can insert `Admissions::from(Admission::new(&policy, Admitted::allowed(..)))` before the layer; the layer appends to it and a handler reads a fabricated admission for a policy no layer evaluated. Compiles; no runtime guard (contrast: the batter-runlimit boundary removes an inbound `Authenticated

`, crates/batter-runlimit/src/http.rs:471). A handler extracting `Extension` on a route without the layer compiles and fails at runtime with 500. ## Proposed remediation Sealed capability: make the four constructors crate-private, carry a private marker in the collection so only this crate's layers append, and have the layer replace an inbound collection it did not create. No workspace caller outside the crate uses the constructors (crates/, examples/, consumers/, runlimit/smoke checked at the snapshot). ## Public hard cut Yes: four public constructors removed; the `batter::runlimit::native_transport::axum` surface changes. Breaking: entry in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md with before/after, `Migration:` rustdoc on `Admissions` naming `Admissions::new`/`push` and `Admission::new`, no shim (the constructors are the forgery path). ## Verification Existing: runlimit/runlimit-axum/tests/layer.rs (`stacked_layers_record_every_admission_in_evaluation_order`, `identical_policy_layers_keep_both_admissions_and_lookup_the_outermost`). New: a test that an inbound forged `Admissions` is discarded; `compile_fail` doctests for `Admission::new` and `Admissions::push`. Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Only runlimit-axum layers can create or append Admission entries; an inbound forged collection is discarded, with a test proving it; compile_fail doctests cover the removed constructors; stacked-layer ordering tests pass unchanged; Breaking: CHANGELOG, Migration: rustdoc and shim decision recorded.

fields.title: Assess typed protected-route registration for the Authenticated principal extractor
fields.description:
## Finding (ADP-3, H04 authenticate phase; Implicit; public) `Authenticated

` is a request-extension phase marker: installed after successful authentication (crates/batter-runlimit/src/http.rs:509), any pre-existing value removed (http.rs:471), and extracted with a 500 when absent (http.rs:83-98). Nothing links the `P` of `HttpQuota::prepare` to the extractors handlers declare. ## Representable but invalid A `PublicProbes` handler or any route outside `prepare` can declare `Authenticated

`; a protected handler can declare `Authenticated` for the wrong principal type. Both compile and fail at runtime with 500. ## Deliverable An ADR-010 assessment with a recorded decision: Axum extractor types cannot be verified against route registration at compile time, so either (a) a typed `ProtectedRoutes

` builder consumed by `prepare` that carries `P` into route registration (public cut of the `Router` parameter; still cannot check extractor generics), or (b) record the obligation as upstream-limited, give the extractor a distinct, documented rejection separate from the three boundary codes, and add a failure test for `Authenticated

` declared on a public probe. Record which option is chosen and why. ## Verification Existing: crates/batter-runlimit/tests/http.rs (`forged_principal_cannot_claim_authentication_or_quota_execution`, `inner_raw_principal_extension_cannot_replace_authenticated_extractor`). New: failure test for the extractor on a public probe. Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: A recorded ADR-010 decision with evidence: either a typed protected-route builder ships with its Breaking: entry, or the extractor-on-unprotected-route case is recorded as upstream-limited with a distinct documented rejection and a failure test; crates/batter-runlimit/AGENTS.md states the remaining obligation.

fields.title: Pass one typed admitted capability through the protected quota boundary and delete unreachable rejections
fields.description:
## Finding (ADP-2, ADP-4, H04 residue; Protocol with Implicit markers; private, wire codes)
The protected boundary reads `OperationContext` (crates/batter-runlimit/src/http.rs:472-474), `expect`s `RequestInterruptionResponder` (http.rs:475-479), reads `ConnectInfo` (480-486) and takes `QuotaRecorder` (487-489), rejecting with `BoundaryRejection::{MissingContext, MissingPeer, MissingObserver}` (http.rs:411-439) that `prepare` (http.rs:343-366) and both registration paths make unreachable: they are defensive states the native guide says to delete rather than document, yet they are published as `missing_context`, `missing_peer`, `missing_observer` wire codes. In crates/batter-runlimit/src/quota.rs:281-291 and 331-334 the `interrupted_check` latch (`NotStarted` to `InFlight`) is a second encoding of the transition that `CheckObservation::start()` already performs (quota/observation.rs:26-34), left by the batter-jnjj remediation.

## Proposed remediation
Extract one typed admitted capability (`batter_axum::AdmittedRequest` already records context and responder, crates/batter-axum/src/low_level.rs:279) and carry the peer and quota recorder through middleware state or the same capability, then delete the three rejection arms, the `expect` and their wire codes. Derive `InterruptedCheck` from the consumed observation owner (for example `start()` returning the started owner plus a `Copy` witness the outer match consumes) and delete the latch.

## Public hard cut
No Rust API cut; removes three documented HTTP codes: CHANGELOG entry and the response-contract table in docs/integrations.md (if present) and crates/batter-runlimit/AGENTS.md.

## Verification
Existing: tests/http/response_contract.rs (`fixed_quota_rejections_have_stable_codes_and_no_store` does not pin the Missing* codes), tests/quota.rs (`unresolved_quota_timeout_drops_backend_and_never_starts_work`, `never_polled_and_pre_cancelled_do_no_backend_or_factory_work`). New: a test proving every `prepare` composition installs all boundary capabilities before the handler, then deletion of the dead arms.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The boundary obtains context, responder, peer and recorder through typed capabilities with no defensive Missing* arms, expect or wire codes; the interrupted_check latch is gone and the interruption classification derives from the consumed observation owner; the quota interruption tests and HTTP response-contract tests pass; the removed codes are recorded in the CHANGELOG and integration docs.

fields.title: Make attempt abandonment an explicit transition with one exhaustive observer
fields.description:
## Finding (ADP-5, ADP-6, L07; Protocol and Mixed; public behaviour, private emitter)
In the protected runner the `PgAttemptReceipt` lives across verification (crates/batter-runlimit/src/attempts.rs:334-348); on `AttemptError::Verification(V)` it is dropped and "remains active until native expiry, which conservatively counts abandonment" (attempts.rs:198-200). Native defines `AttemptOutcome::Abandoned` (runlimit/runlimit-core/src/attempts.rs:166) and `PostgresAttemptLimiter::complete` accepts a receipt, but the runner never emits an abandonment and `AttemptObservation` has no abandonment event. The observer is held twice (`AttemptRunner.observer`, attempts.rs:269, and inside `PostgresAttemptLimiter` via `with_observer`, 298-302); native emits Admitted/Denied while the runner emits Completed/Stale/CommitUncertain through a match with a `_ => None` arm (attempts.rs:401-416), contradicting the native "every dispatch point is exhaustive" rule.

## Representable but invalid
Nothing compile-wise. An operational verification failure keeps the subject Busy for the whole lease with no explicit transition or observation; an `AttemptError` variant added on either side is silently unobserved.

## Proposed remediation
On `Verification(V)` (not on interruption, which stays conservative) run a bounded native `complete(receipt, Abandoned)` or make the choice an explicit `AttemptRunner` policy, and add the observation. Give the observer one owner: either pass it into the native limiter once and let the native low-level seam emit completion, or keep all emission in the runner, with an exhaustive match over `AttemptError`. Coordinate with the transaction-owned low-level task and the shared attempt transition task.

## Public hard cut
No if additive; a new `AttemptObservation` variant is a semver-signaled addition recorded in runlimit/CHANGELOG.md.

## Verification
Existing (live): crates/batter-runlimit/tests/attempts_live.rs (`cancelled_verification_keeps_busy_lease_without_open_application_transaction`, `application_error_rolls_back_audit_and_does_not_reset_reservation`, `acknowledged_commit_survives_observer_cancellation_at_publication`). New: verification failure leads to explicit abandonment and re-admission after backoff; a test enumerating every `AttemptError` variant against the emitted event.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: A verification failure produces an explicit, observed abandonment transition (or a recorded explicit runner policy), interruption stays conservative, the attempt observer has one owner with an exhaustive match over AttemptError and no wildcard arm, and the new and named live tests pass.

fields.title: Validate maintenance budgets once and refuse repeated public-probe registration
fields.description:
## Finding (ADP-7, ADP-8; Protocol and Implicit builder phase; public constructors)
`ExpiryMaintenance::new` validates `PeriodicPolicy::new(interval, interval, ..)` with a placeholder budget (crates/batter-runlimit/src/maintenance.rs:185-187); `register_in` derives the real budget and `expect`s a second validation (maintenance.rs:216-222, 396). Sound today only because `PeriodicPolicy::new` checks positivity alone and native timeouts are bounded; a future relation check would turn registration into a panic. `HttpQuota::with_public_probes` overwrites `public_probes: Option<PublicProbes>` (crates/batter-runlimit/src/http.rs:209, 305-308), so a second call silently drops the first set; a GET collision with a protected route panics inside Axum's merge at `prepare` (http.rs:320-323), which is upstream behaviour.

## Proposed remediation
Validate the periodic policy once where the budget is known (in `register_in`, returning a typed error) or build it from the limiter configuration at construction, and delete the `expect`. Merge or reject a second `with_public_probes` call. Record the GET collision as upstream (Axum router) behaviour.

## Public hard cut
Only if `register_in`'s error type changes; record accordingly.

## Verification
Existing: tests/maintenance.rs (`registration_is_inert_and_validates_its_name`, `native_timeouts_classify_a_hung_acquisition_before_the_run_deadline`), tests/http/response_contract.rs (`protected_get_colliding_with_public_probe_panics_during_prepare`, `public_probe_registration_rejects_route_patterns`). New: a second `with_public_probes` call is merged or rejected with a test.

Source snapshot: 986d294. Parent catalog and policy: bead show batter-ctk7 --json.
fields.acceptance_criteria: ExpiryMaintenance validates its periodic policy exactly once with no expect at registration; a repeated with_public_probes call is merged or rejected with a test; the GET collision is recorded as upstream behaviour; maintenance and response-contract tests pass.
